problemStatement.formal: For variables indexed by Fin n over a commutative ring, define power sums and elementary symmetric polynomials, then derive Newton identities via MvPolynomial evaluation.
problemStatement.plain: Generalizes Newton identities and Vieta-style coefficient relations from small fixed arities to n variables using Mathlib's MvPolynomial symmetric-polynomial infrastructure.
whyMatters: Newton identities are the bridge between power sums of roots and elementary symmetric coefficients.
Moving from hand-written low-degree cases to Fin n makes the Vieta machinery reusable for arbitrary finite families.
The proof demonstrates how Mathlib's abstract symmetric-polynomial theorems can be evaluated into concrete formulas.

proven: Concrete powerSum and elemSymm definitions are provided for functions Fin n -> R.
Evaluation bridges connect MvPolynomial.psum and MvPolynomial.esymm to the concrete definitions (Lean: aeval_psum_eq and aeval_esymm_eq).
General Newton identities are derived from Mathlib symmetric-polynomial theorems (Lean: newton_identity and newton_identity_psum).
Basic elementary-symmetric and power-sum identities are included, including newton_first.
Two-, three-, and four-variable specializations plus Vieta product formulas are verified by ring.
knownResults.goal: Document the verified n-variable Newton-identity generalization and its Vieta-formula specializations.
